listing.aiSummary: Automates colony management including building construction, resource distribution, and crisis response.

description:
Jonah's Colony Manager
Automatic Colony Management, the mod.

Source code and guides
Required mods: none
Updating: delete the old Jonah's Colony Manager folder in mods/ and extract the new one. Safe mid-save, settings stay with the save. MagicLib (Version Checker is built in) or TriOS tells you about new versions.
Safe to add mid-game

Breaks saves if removed

No known mod conflicts

Short summary
Set a colony to Auto and the mod manages it: buildings, item and AI core placement, administrators and crises.
Every action costs what it would cost you, plus a small fee you can change.
Long description
I like having tons of colonies and the limits off, and I kept getting in over my head managing them. So I had Claude Code make this.

Hit the Colony Autopilot button on the colony screen (or right click Population & Infrastructure) and pick a mode. Everything is editable on the fly from the Colony Autopilot tab in the intel screen.

It starts on Advisor, so nothing happens until you switch to Approve or Auto. I'd use Approve or Advisor unless you want to go fully hands-off. I play on Auto.

Items and AI cores go in Autopilot Storage at any colony, and it ships them where they're needed for a fee and some travel time.

I'm also working on a story version where you unlock the functions slowly with AI cores. It's still early.

Features
Builds and upgrades on its own
Follows a plan for each planet within your budget and keeps colonies off 0 stability. Items, AI cores and administrators
Puts your items and cores where they do the most, and hires and places administrators.
Autopilot Storage
Drop items and AI cores into Autopilot Storage at any colony. It ships them where they're needed for a fee and some travel time. Your capital
One colony becomes your home port and, later, a trade hub.
Stations and stable locations
Colonies get stations as they grow, and relays, buoys and arrays go up at stable locations. Threats and colony crises
Plans security when a colony is in danger and prices crises into what it builds. Optional: the Low profile expansion style lowers the odds of inspections, Pather cells and raids.
Surplus and the endgame
Spends large surpluses. In the endgame economy it builds for production, research and military over income. War, with Nexerelin
Defense fleets, pirate base strikes, hitting back at raiders, and agents. Invasions are left to you.
Research, terraforming and more
Runs research, terraforming, trade contracts and megastructures when their mods are installed. Plays fair
It leaves game balance alone, pays fees and waits out travel time like you would.
Short on-screen lines
Each action shows as a short line like BUILD / Hot Springs: Planetary Shield (750k). The log has the full text. Settings
Colony Autopilot button on the colony screen, and a tab in the intel screen. Modes: Advisor (default), Approve, Auto. Every setting
Mod integrations
Supports 20+ colony mods. None are required. Full list in the Supported mods spoiler below. Checkable
The audit page lists everything it can change and what it costs.

Getting started
Open a colony and hit Colony Autopilot.
Pick a goal, or leave it on Balanced.
Set the mode to Auto and save the recommended setup.
Drop items and AI cores into Autopilot Storage.

Heads up: Auto starts building right away. Try Advisor or Approve first, or back up your save.
Guides: getting started | how it builds | money and the endgame | war and security | items and cores | what it does with each mod | roadmap

Coming in 3.0
Built, in testing: a new build planner. One ranked build queue for all colonies, a 36-month payback limit, and removed buildings stay off that colony's build list for a year.
Planned: a money ladder that spends spare credits on stockpiles, growth, military, ships and new colonies, in that order.
Planned: auto-expansion through Nexerelin colony expeditions. One setting, off by default.
Planned: one war level for the empire and a stance for each faction, from Ally to Destroy.
Planned: a settings menu of about 20 main rows.
Back up your save before updating. A save made in 3.0 can't be loaded in 2.45.x.

Plans can still change. Full roadmap

Supported mods
All optional, each one turns on by itself when its mod is enabled.
Terraforming Made Easy: special-world plans (Forge, Fortress, Paradise, Hive, Death, Waste) and terraforming, Domain-era upgrades for comm relays, nav buoys and sensor arrays
Forum thread
Industrial Evolution: ambassadors, edicts, VPC chips, specialized mining and refining, courier shipping
Forum thread
Nexerelin: defense, relief and war fleets (never invasions), agents, sieges, the Derelict Empire start
Forum thread
Ashes of the Domain (Vaults of Knowledge, Theory of Toolbox, Building Menu Overhaul): research, research locks, synergies, management styles, trade contracts, production orders, special projects, megastructures, wonders and gates, Hypershunt Receivers
Ashes of the Domain (Vaults of Knowledge, Theory of Toolbox) | Building Menu Overhaul
Emergent Threats (IX Revival): Antimatter Stabilizer conversion, Panopticon cores into the Surveillance Center
Forum thread
Random Assortment of Things: Frontiers settlement
Forum thread
Station Augments: best augment loadout per station, the Mining Station augment, economic in well-defended systems
Forum thread
Interstellar Imperium and Knights of Ludd: their stations count like vanilla ones, plus the Imperium station line
Interstellar Imperium | Knights of Ludd
Terraforming & Station Construction (Boggled): its terraforming projects and the buildings they need, mining and siphon stations founded as new colonies (optional)
Forum thread
Grand.Colonies: builds past 12 buildings, with the extra upkeep counted
Forum thread
Substance.Abuse: Breweries and recipes
Forum thread
Volkov Industrial Conglomerate: viral contamination treatment first, soil nanites only on vanilla farmland
Forum thread
Roider Union: Dives and Union HQ valued by what they mine nearby beyond what the colony already makes, Roider Charters placed
Forum thread
Planetary Shield: Access Control: the shield valued as defense, port kept closed with Pather cells
Forum thread
Unknown Skies, What We Left Behind, Astral Ascension: their mining conditions and water worlds, planetless colonies kept safe
Unknown Skies | What We Left Behind | Astral Ascension
Omega Core Everywhere and Astral Ascension Renewed: Omega cores go where they do the most, in a building or as an administrator
Omega Core Everywhere | Astral Ascension Renewed
Niko's Scavengable Industries: builds the blueprints you know, the risky ones are left to you
Forum thread
Junk Yard Dogs and Carter's Freetraders: resource forges and the Biolab, with illegal goods counted right
Junk Yard Dogs | Carter's Freetraders
Vulpoids: Organ Farms, the Biotech Facility, its colony items and Profecto administrators (the Vulpoid Bioforge story is left to you)
Forum thread
Yunru Industries, Yunru's Worlds and Slightly Better Tech-Mining: Secondary Drydocks, Auxiliary Shipbays, richer Tech-Mining
Yunru's mod thread (all three)
United Aurora Federation: its colony items placed by what they actually do
Forum thread
Jonah's Auto Outfitting: plans producers for the goods its big weapon orders need
GitHub
Any other mod: its deposits and colony items through the game's own tables, and its buildings measured on a test colony
Cloning (Oddisz): the three cloning industries built when faster growth is worth it, with room for the stability penalty to grow
Forum thread
Reverse Engineered Private Arsenal (Oddisz): left to you; never built or taken down, its core and Drone Replicator never moved
Forum thread
Sol Renewed (Oddisz): industries in Sol priced for what they add to its crisis meter, meter on the Crises page
Forum thread
Toolbox Economy Curves and Coalesced Little Mods (Oddisz): the curve you pick is planned with as is; the pack gets the same handling as Cloning and the Private Arsenal
Forum thread | GitHub

Checked and fine as they are, nothing needed: Better Colonies, Supply Forging, LOST_SECTOR, Kon's Player Faction Bundles, Galactic Constellate, Tri-Tachyon Expansion, Luddic Enhancement, Hillock, Hazard Mining, Hiver Swarm, Adversary, Gambling Den, Extra System Reloaded - Oddisz Edition, Hullmods - Renewed, Intel Renewed, StopBloatingMe, StopStackingMe, StarterPack, Discord Rich Presence.
If you would like one added please let me know here or in the GitHub issues and I'll do it asap.

Compatibility and permissions
Compatibility and known issues
Optional integrations: Nexerelin, Ashes of the Domain, Terraforming Made Easy, Industrial Evolution, Random Assortment of Things, Station Augments, Emergent Threats and more (Supported mods, above)
Tested with: my 90-ish mod list. Every release is checked offline against every combination of the supported mods.
Known conflicts: none that I know of
Known issues: expect bugs. Report them here or as GitHub issues, ideally with starsector-core/starsector.log, saves/common/colony_autopilot_diagnostics.json.data and your modlist. Permissions
Code: use it however you want. Modpacks, reuploads, forks, all fine, no need to ask or credit me. Just don't sell it.
Assets: there's no art in the mod

FAQ
Will it mess with my save if I add it mid-game?
No. It starts on Advisor, so nothing happens until you pick Approve or Auto. Don't remove it later, because the Autopilot Storage tab lives on your markets.

Does it cheat?
No. Everything costs what it would cost you, plus a fee you can change, and shipping and hiring take travel time.

I don't want colony crises. Can it avoid them?
Mostly. Pick Low profile, or switch it under Settings, Expansion style. Pirates and the Persean League come from colony size alone, but it gets you ready for them.

It isn't building anything. Why?
Check the mode (Advisor only advises) and the budget. The getting started guide has a section on it.

Will you add more?
Yep. Ask here or on GitHub if you want a mod supported. A story version is in the works too.

AI use disclaimer
Some or all assets and code in this mod were created using AI tools:
Code: Claude Opus 5.5 (through Claude Code)
Docs, patch notes and the offline build checks: Claude Opus 5.5

No additional training data. There's no art in the mod. I came up with what it should do and tested it in my own games; the AI wrote the code and checks it offline against every combination of the supported mods before each release.

Made by Jonah's Tools | More: Jonah's Auto Outfitting | all my mods on GitHub

Thanks for playing!

The system operates within game balance constraints, charging fees and respecting travel times for all actions.
